A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RL-SMC, SMCTS and TSMCTS research, despite the changed title and format. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments across five environments, including learning curves, runtime comparisons, variance measurements and ablations in Figures 1–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for the retained environments, expanded baseline and hybrid comparisons, and additional SMCTS learning curves in Figures 1–5.

M1.justification: The central search construction is retained, but the written final-policy procedure changes: v1 Algorithm 4 includes Gumbel noise in the returned policy, whereas v2 Equation 26 and Algorithm 3 use the unperturbed prior. v2 also introduces TSMCTS+TRT, incorporating trust-region machinery and revived resampling that v1 only described as compatible extensions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Snake-v1, Rubikscube-partly-scrambled-v0, Ant, Halfcheetah and Humanoid. The added comparisons and learning curves retain this discrete and continuous task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 2 adds full TRT-SMC and TSMCTS+TRT comparisons; v1 evaluated only a TRT-inspired degeneracy-control variant in its diagnostic analysis. The main comparison also uses the original SPO implementation where available, while retaining the SMC baseline in Appendix C. GumbelAZ corresponds to the earlier GumbelMCTS-based agent rather than a newly added baseline.

E3.justification: v1 describes a common AZ setup differing only in the planner. v2 makes an exception for the original SPO implementation, retaining the explicitly shared setup for TSMCTS, TRT-SMC and GumbelAZ. The main N=4, T=6 and MCTS B=24 budgets and most tabulated settings remain unchanged; newly disclosed diagnostic controls do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: v2 tests whether TSMCTS benefits from incorporating TRT components and adds per-environment SMCTS-versus-TSMCTS learning curves at N=4, T=6 in Figure 5. These extend the component analysis. The depth, variance, degeneracy and m1 sensitivity analyses already existed in v1, despite their relocation and renumbering.

E5.justification: Learning curves, runtime comparisons, depth-performance curves and m1 sensitivity plots switch from 90% BCa-bootstrap intervals to 95% Gaussian intervals. The variance and degeneracy panels already used approximately 95% Gaussian intervals. Corresponding experiments retain their stated 20-, 10- and 5-seed counts; no increase in those counts is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds full TRT-SMC, TSMCTS+TRT and per-environment SMCTS results, including evidence that TRT components benefit TSMCTS on Rubikscube and Halfcheetah. Retained curves also change: the reported TSMCTS Halfcheetah endpoint at five million interactions is approximately 4,800 in v1 Figure 1 versus 4,200 in v2 Figure 2. The new original-implementation SPO curves should not be treated as same-setting updates to the earlier SMC baseline.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 2 and Lemma 1 with proofs concerning improvement using an improved policy's values and mixtures of improved policies. Theorem 1 and its corollary now specify greedification operators rather than general improvement operators. Appendix A also adds the explicit CAI-SMC recovery derivation, stationarity reasoning and revised variance assumptions; the existing complexity conclusions remain.

C1.justification: v2 expands the introduction's comparative claims to SPO and full TRT-SMC and explicitly frames the contribution as a search-based policy-improvement operator. The principal claims about improved depth scaling, reduced variance, mitigated path degeneracy and retained parallelization properties remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a stationarity-based justification for sequential halving and qualifies variance arguments with equal-return-variance assumptions and the assumption that the improved policy does not increase variance. It also discusses off-policy reuse through refreshed search targets and a possible advantage of larger m1 at high depth budgets. These extend the retained mechanism explanations and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 expands ancestor/resampling bookkeeping, continuous-policy details, baseline implementation provenance and the disclosure that diagnostic planners share DNNs. It removes the named cluster/GPU models and the commitment to release code upon acceptance. Its revised value-loss Equation 55 targets Vsearch directly, while surrounding prose and Algorithm 4 retain TD-lambda targets, leaving the intended implementation ambiguous.

R1.justification: v2 adds broader SMC-for-RL references, including Lazaric, Hoffman, Le and Abdulsamad, plus connections to inverse-variance weighting, bandit assumptions and off-policy reanalysis. It removes the ancestor-sampling comparison associated with Lindsten. The updated publication details for Value Improved Actor Critic Algorithms refer to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and substantial portions of the background, method explanations and experimental narrative are rewritten. Experiments now begin with scaling and diagnostic evidence, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded. The standalone reproducibility, LLM-usage and acknowledgment sections disappear, while a generic impact statement is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two, with extensively resized and rearranged figures. The m1 plot moves into the main text, runtime plots move to Appendix C, the main benchmark figure gains additional series, and Figure 5 is added. Legends, colors, captions and panel ordering change, and the six hyperparameter tables are consolidated onto one page.

improvement.justification: The full TRT-SMC comparisons, hybrid tests and SMCTS learning curves strengthen empirical support. However, the new Appendix A.3 proofs rely on identities that do not generally hold: Equation 44 substitutes a different continuation policy's value, and Equation 51 treats statewise policy mixtures as linear mixtures of values. Removed hardware disclosures and conflicting value-target documentation also weaken reproducibility. These substantive benefits and drawbacks prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
